claims.text: Machine learning-based optimization of processing parameters can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in aluminum alloys.
Machine learning optimization can increase elongation at break by 20% relative to conventionally processed aluminum alloys.
Machine learning optimization can increase yield strength by 15% relative to conventionally processed aluminum alloys.
The proposed improvements are achieved by optimizing the alloy microstructure and properties.
Prior hot rolling or forging leaves the conventional aluminum-alloy baseline with reduced ductility.
The relevant aluminum alloys contain 90-99% aluminum.
A combination of decision trees and neural networks can predict optimal processing parameters from material composition, microstructure, material-property data, and processing-condition data.
The applicable processing-pressure range is 100-500 MPa.
Grain size, phase distribution, and defect density affect the strength and ductility of the aluminum alloys.
Predictive optimization balances strength and ductility by minimizing defect density.
Predictive optimization balances strength and ductility by maximizing grain-boundary cohesion.
Machine-learning models can identify processing parameters that balance strength and ductility from a database of properties and processing conditions.
The optimized processing parameters are applicable to aluminum alloys processed by hot rolling or forging.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts specific gains of 20% in elongation and 15% in yield strength, but the falsification rule only rejects sufficiently large reductions or an undefined trade-off ratio. Results far below the predicted gains could therefore fail to falsify the stated hypothesis.
